title: Image Cytometry-Based Quantification of Human Pulmonary Arterial Endothelial Cells
author: Ibrahim, Moinuddin, et al.

steps.title: Obtain approvals and prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Secure institutional and ethical approvals for working with primary human pulmonary arterial cells, prepare all supplements, growth media, and buffers in advance, and ensure access to an image‑based cellular cytometer (e.g., Celigo, Cytation, or Molecular Devices PICO) capable of detecting Hoechst (Ex ≈ 350 nm, Em ≈ 461 nm) and Propidium Iodide (Ex ≈ 535 nm, Em ≈ 617 nm). Verify that the cytometer software supports viability and nuclear‑staining analysis.

substeps.instruction: Obtain institutional and ethical clearance for human PACs.
Prepare supplements, growth media, and buffers before receiving cells.
Confirm availability of a compatible image‑based cytometer.
Check software for cell‑viability and nuclear‑stain quantification tools.

steps.title: Fabricate or obtain PDMS microfluidic chips
steps.instruction: Design, mold, fabricate, and sterilize five‑channel PDMS chips with hexagonal pillar structures, then store them sterile for up to 2 weeks (or 4 weeks at 4 °C with re‑plasma before use).

substeps.instruction: Design the chip in CAD (e.g., SolidWorks) with five channels and hexagonal pillars; optional design service: Parallel Fluidics.
Submit the 3D design to a photomask manufacturer (e.g., Artnetpro Inc.). A typical 11"×14" 20K mask costs ≈ $146.50.
Clean a silicon wafer with compressed air.
Spin‑coat SU‑8 2100 photoresist to achieve ~150 µm thickness.
Soft‑bake the coated wafer for 1 h at the recommended temperature.
Align the photomask onto the photoresist side and expose to UV (UV‑KUB 2) for ~10 min.
Second soft‑bake for 2.5 h.
Develop in SU‑8 developer for ~8 min until patterns are clear; rinse with isopropanol for ≥30 s.
Dry both wafer sides with compressed air until no residues remain.
Inspect microscopically for sharp edges, linear channels, and correct geometry.
Create a master mold: place wafer in a sterile petri dish, tape corners, seal lid.
Mix PDMS base and curing agent at a 10:1 ratio, degas under vacuum.
Pour PDMS onto the master mold and cure at 80 °C for 2 h.
Cool, then peel cured PDMS from the mold.
Cut individual chips and punch inlet/outlet ports with a biopsy punch.
Plasma‑bond PDMS chips to sterile glass slides; trim excess glass with a diamond cutter.
Place bonded chips in a 65 °C incubator for 2 h, then cure at 80 °C for 1 h.
Autoclave at 121 °C, 15 psi for 20–30 min if sterilization is required; cool in a biosafety cabinet.
Store sterilized chips at 20‑25 °C in sealed sterile petri dishes for ≤2 weeks, or at 4 °C for ≤4 weeks. Re‑plasma if stored >1 week.

steps.title: Prepare humidifying chamber for chips
steps.instruction: Create a custom humidity chamber using an autoclaved pipette box filled with sterile water; place UV‑sterilized microfluidic chips inside the box to maintain a humid environment during cell seeding and incubation.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave a pipette box.
Fill the lower compartment with sterile, autoclaved water.
Place UV‑sterilized chips onto the box surface inside the sterile hood.

steps.title: Seed PAH‑ECs into microfluidic chips
steps.instruction: Prepare a PAH‑EC suspension at 10 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ (5 × 10⁵ cells in 50 µL medium), introduce 10 µL into the middle channel of each chip, incubate for cell attachment, add culture medium, and maintain chips in the humid chamber for 5–7 days with daily imaging.

substeps.instruction: Split PAH‑ECs according to standard pulmonary arterial cell culture protocols.
Prepare cell suspension: 10 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹; typically 5 × 10⁵ cells in 50 µL medium.
Using a P10 pipette, gently resuspend the suspension, aspirate 10 µL, insert tip into the inlet of the chip’s middle channel, and slowly dispense until the suspension reaches the outlet.
Incubate chips at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ≥6 h to allow attachment; confirm attachment microscopically.
After attachment, add sufficient culture medium to all channels and reservoirs.
Return chips to the custom humidifying chamber and continue incubation at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 5–7 days.
Stain and acquire images every 24 h as described in later steps.

steps.title: Stain cells with nuclear dyes
steps.instruction: Prepare a 2 mL staining solution containing 1 µg mL⁻¹ propidium iodide and 5 µg mL⁻¹ Hoechst in PBS, add 500 µL to each chip, protect from light, incubate 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, then wash with 500 µL PBS if background is high.

substeps.instruction: Dilute PI stock and Hoechst stock in PBS to achieve final concentrations of 1 µg mL⁻¹ PI and 5 µg mL⁻¹ Hoechst; total volume 2 mL.
Using a micropipette, add 500 µL of the mixed dye solution into the designated channels of each chip.
Ensure even coverage of all cells and wrap the device in aluminum foil to protect from light.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 30 min.
If background fluorescence is excessive, gently wash the chip with 500 µL PBS to remove excess dye.

steps.title: Create imaging protocol in CellReporterXpress
steps.instruction: Launch CellReporterXpress, add a new protocol based on the “Live‑dead assay (cell integration)” template, verify device connection, set plate type, stains, objective, well locations, and focus parameters (e.g., DAPI +71 µm offset, 500 µs; TRITC 0 µm offset, 10 µs).

substeps.instruction: Open CellReporterXpress on the computer; the landing page shows Acquisition, Experiments, Monitor, Configuration, Devices.
Click “Acquisition”, then “Add Protocol”.
Select the template “Live‑dead assay (cell integration)”.
Verify the cytometer is online (green circle).
In Acquisition Settings, click the first icon to choose the 6‑well plate template.
Click the second icon to select stains: DAPI (Hoechst; Ex/Em ≈ 350/461 nm) and TRITC (PI; Ex/Em ≈ 535/617 nm).
Click the third icon to select the 4× objective lens.
Specify wells containing chips (e.g., well A1).
Open focus settings, choose plate‑bottom focus method, use DAPI channel to set focus (example: +71 µm offset, 500 µs exposure).
Fine‑tune focus for TRITC (example: 0 µm offset, 10 µs exposure) and capture a snapshot to confirm image quality.

steps.title: Set region and analysis parameters
steps.instruction: Define the imaging region (full well or ROI), add a 2‑channel cell‑scoring analysis with DAPI as nuclei and TRITC as dead‑cell channel, and set initial intensity threshold 40, minimum width 8, maximum width 40; save settings and add the region for automatic analysis.

substeps.instruction: Click the third prompt to select the image acquisition area; choose full well or draw a square ROI manually or automatically.
Click the fourth prompt to open “Choose Analysis”; select a 2‑channel cell‑scoring analysis.
Assign DAPI as channel 1 (nuclei) and TRITC as channel 2 (PI, dead cells).
Set initial segmentation parameters: intensity threshold = 40, minimum width = 8, maximum width = 40 (adjust as needed).
Save these analysis settings with a descriptive name.
Click the fifth prompt to add the captured image region for automatic analysis.

steps.title: Select wells, save, and run protocol
steps.instruction: Choose the wells to image, keep default imaging order, save the protocol with a clear name, then start the run and monitor its status until completion.

substeps.instruction: Use the sixth prompt to select which wells to image and analyze.
Skip the optional temperature‑controlled acquisition (seventh prompt) and keep default imaging direction/order (eighth prompt).
Click the ninth prompt to save the protocol; provide a name such as “Live‑Dead Microfluidic Assay”.
Click the tenth prompt, enter an experiment name and details, and press the “Play” button to start acquisition.
Monitor the run on the Monitor page (statuses: In Progress, Failed, Succeeded).
When the run shows “Succeeded”, return to the landing page (house icon) and click “Experiments” to view images and analyzed data.

steps.title: Reanalyse data and export results
steps.instruction: If needed, adjust analysis thresholds, re‑run analysis, then export cell count and PI‑positive data to Excel; optionally export images for presentation.

substeps.instruction: From the CellReporterXpress landing page, click “Experiments” and locate the completed experiment.
Open the experiment; select the “Analyses” tab, then “Measurements”.
Choose parameters to export (e.g., total cells, PI‑positive cells) and click “Export” to generate an Excel (.xlsx) file.
If image export is required, switch to “Plate View”, review images, and export as needed.
Process the exported data in GraphPad Prism or other analysis software.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of cell counts
steps.instruction: Plot cell‑count data using GraphPad Prism (v10.1.2), using the number of independent chip imaging repetitions as the sample size (n).
